pr.title: Added query per subscription and queryKeys along with the messages

## What does this PR do?

Issue
Currently , query getting set at the connection level during subscriptions resulting in overwriting of the queries and multiple subscriptions creating unexpected results

Solution
Setting at the subscription level with querykeys resulting query per subscription

Note
* Multiple subscription with different queries results in merging of the querykeys as the websocket connection id is one per client. 
* So to differentiate between two subscriptions, it must be done in the sdk subscription() level only. To help this out and proper distinction the queryKeys are also sent with the response.

Usage
Sdk subscription methods should use the query keys to filter out what message to pass to the onMessage callback of the subscription

subscription1 receives all the query keys with ''

## Walkthrough

Subscriptions now store per-connection query-key maps per channel (queries normalized to query keys; empty queries use the empty-string key). Connection records no longer store raw queries. The messaging adapter’s subscribe/unsubscribe/hasSubscriber/getSubscribers were updated to use the new query-key mapping and return a mapping of receiverId → matched queryKeys. Realtime transport switched from bulk sends to per-connection sends that include the matched subscription IDs/queryKeys and increment a totalMessages telemetry counter. Realtime::subscribe signature was changed to accept a `subscriptionId`; new helpers `constructSubscriptions` and `getSubscriptionMetadata` were introduced. E2E and unit tests were added/updated for query-key behavior.

class RuntimeQuery extends Query
{
    public const ALLOWED_QUERIES = [
        // Equality & comparison
        Query::TYPE_EQUAL,
        Query::TYPE_NOT_EQUAL,
        Query::TYPE_LESSER,
        Query::TYPE_LESSER_EQUAL,
        Query::TYPE_GREATER,
        Query::TYPE_GREATER_EQUAL,

        // Null checks
        Query::TYPE_IS_NULL,
        Query::TYPE_IS_NOT_NULL,

        // Recursive checks
        Query::TYPE_AND,
        Query::TYPE_OR
    ];

    /**
     * `@param` array<Query> $queries
     * `@param` array<string, mixed> $payload
     */
    public static function filter(array $queries, array $payload): array
    {
        if (empty($queries)) {
            return $payload;
        }
        // multiple queries follows and condition
        foreach ($queries as $query) {
            if (!self::evaluateFilter($query, $payload)) {
                return [];
            };
        }
        return $payload;
    }

    private static function evaluateFilter(Query $query, array $payload): bool
    {
        $attribute = $query->getAttribute();
        $method = $query->getMethod();
        $values = $query->getValues();

        // during 'and' and 'or' attribute will not be present
        switch ($method) {
            case Query::TYPE_AND:
                // All subqueries must evaluate to true
                foreach ($query->getValues() as $subquery) {
                    if (!self::evaluateFilter($subquery, $payload)) {
                        return false;
                    }
                }
                return true;

            case Query::TYPE_OR:
                // At least one subquery must evaluate to true
                foreach ($query->getValues() as $subquery) {
                    if (self::evaluateFilter($subquery, $payload)) {
                        return true;
                    }
                }
                return false;
        }

        $hasAttribute = \array_key_exists($attribute, $payload);
        if (!$hasAttribute) {
            return false;
        }

        // null can be a value as well
        $payloadAttributeValue = $payload[$attribute];
        switch ($method) {
            case Query::TYPE_EQUAL:
                return self::anyMatch($values, fn ($value) => $payloadAttributeValue === $value);

            case Query::TYPE_NOT_EQUAL:
                return !self::anyMatch($values, fn ($value) => $payloadAttributeValue === $value);

            case Query::TYPE_LESSER:
                return self::anyMatch($values, fn ($value) => $payloadAttributeValue < $value);

            case Query::TYPE_LESSER_EQUAL:
                return self::anyMatch($values, fn ($value) => $payloadAttributeValue <= $value);

            case Query::TYPE_GREATER:
                return self::anyMatch($values, fn ($value) => $payloadAttributeValue > $value);

            case Query::TYPE_GREATER_EQUAL:
                return self::anyMatch($values, fn ($value) => $payloadAttributeValue >= $value);

                // attribute must be present and should be explicitly null
            case Query::TYPE_IS_NULL:
                return $payloadAttributeValue === null;

            case Query::TYPE_IS_NOT_NULL:
                return $payloadAttributeValue !== null;

            default:
                throw new \InvalidArgumentException(
                    "Unsupported query method: {$method}"
                );
        }
    }

    private static function anyMatch(array $values, callable $fn): bool
    {
        foreach ($values as $value) {
            if ($fn($value)) {
                return true;
            }
        }
        return false;
    }
}

`@ArnabChatterjee20k` You're absolutely right, and I apologize for the confusion. I misunderstood the slot-based subscription architecture.

After reviewing `constructSubscriptions()`, the flow is clear:

1. **Client side**: Subscriptions are grouped by index (slot), e.g., `tests[0][]=select(*)`, `tests[1][]=equal(...)`
2. **Server side**: Each index gets a unique subscription ID via `ID::unique()`, returned as `subscriptions: {0: "sub_abc", 1: "sub_def"}`
3. **SDK mapping**: SDK stores `subscriptionId → callback` (e.g., `{"sub_abc": callback1, "sub_def": callback2}`)
4. **Event routing**: When an event arrives with `subscriptions: ["sub_abc"]`, the SDK looks up and invokes the correct callback

The subscription IDs already uniquely identify which channel+query combination matched, so **queryKeys are indeed redundant**. The SDK can route messages to the correct callbacks using subscription IDs alone.

My original suggestion was incorrect. The current implementation properly supports multiple subscriptions per connection by using subscription IDs as the routing key. Thank you for the clarification! 🙏
